articles.title: Darius Acuff Jr. Joins Rare Lists in NBA History Alongside Jordan, Wilt with Wild Box Score Stats
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. made history with his performance during the team's 132-120 loss to the New Orleans Pelicans on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. made history with his performance during the team's 132-120 loss to the New Orleans Pelicans on Thursday night.

Acuff finished with 34 points, 14 assists, six rebounds and one steal while shooting 13-of-26 from the field and 3-of-11 from three-point territory.

The point guard joined Michael Jordan, Trae Young and Steve Francis as the only rookies to record at least 34 points, 14 assists, six rebounds and one steal in a single game.

Acuff also joined the list of just nine players, including Wilt Chamberlain, to rack up multiple 30-point games within the first five appearances of his career.

Young, Oscar Robertson and Isiah Thomas are the only other players in NBA history with a 30-point, 10-assist performance within their first five games played as well.

Acuff displayed his pull-up shooting potential as well as his athleticism against New Orleans, throwing down a one-handed dunk in transition during the first quarter.

While it's important not to put too much stock into the plus-minus of a single game, it's still worth noting that the Kings outscored the Pelicans by three points in Acuff's 41 minutes on the floor despite ultimately suffering a 12-point defeat.

Sacramento fell to 0-5 with the loss, but the play of the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft has been a silver lining this season.

Acuff is now recording 24.0 points and 6.6 assists per game, with both averages representing the highest marks among all rookies. He's connected on 47.3 percent of his two-point field goal attempts despite struggling from behind the arc, hitting a mere 22.2 percent of his triples.

Acuff will look to help the Kings win their first game of the season as they travel to face the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday.

articles.title: Hawks beat Cavaliers 114-111, winning home game that forced Dream to play WNBA Finals Game 6 in early afternoon
articles.summary: The game that forced the Dream to play WNBA Finals Game 6 during the day at State Farm Arena was a win for the Hawks.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks' third home game of the season at State Farm Arena initially drew attention for forcing the Atlanta Dream to move Game 6 of the WNBA Finals earlier on Thursday to a 12:30 p.m. ET start.

Thankfully for Atlanta and the fans who rearranged their plans on short notice to attend a daytime game, the Dream won 80-69 to force the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history and give themselves an opportunity to win the franchise's first championship.

However, the Hawks also won their first home game of the season after the arena staff changed courts with a 114-111 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night.

Onyeka Okongwu scored 29 points (shooting 4 of 6 on 3-pointers) and grabbed 12 rebounds for the Hawks, who improved their season record to 2-3. Nickeil Alexander-Walker followed with 25 points and Aaron Wiggins provided 20 off the bench, hitting 4 of his 7 3-point attempts.

Playing their second of back-to-back games following a 129-117 loss to the Miami Heat on Wednesday, the Hawks initially looked tired out. The Cavs ran out to a 28-16 lead after the first quarter with James Harden scoring nine points and Sam Merrill adding eight.

However, Atlanta soared back in the second quarter, outscoring Cleveland 30-16. Okongwu and Wiggins each scored eight points, helping the Hawks to go into halftime with a 46-44 lead.

The home team kept up the pressure in the third quarter, beginning with an 11-2 run highlighted by two 3-pointers from Okongwu to put Atlanta ahead 57-46. The Cavaliers chipped away at the Hawks' lead with a Mario Hezonja 3-pointer cutting Cleveland's deficit to 81-79 with 1:50 remaining in the quarter.

Following an Alexander-Walker basket, a 3 from Jarrett Allen pulled the Cavs to within one point. But the Hawks scored the final six points of the quarter to take an 89-82 lead into the fourth.

Late in regulation, a basket and free throw by Harden trimmed Atlanta's lead to 108-104. With under a minute to play, Okongwu fouled Donovan Mitchell on a 3-point shot and the Cavs' star made all three free throws to again cut Cleveland's deficit to one point.

But Okongwu rebounded a missed 3 from Alexander-Walker and scored to put the Hawks ahead by three. Mitchell followed with a floater to again make it a 1-point game, but Alexander-Walker put the game away by making two free throws with 15.3 left in the game. Mitchell missed two 3-pointers in the closing seconds and Atlanta escaped with the win.

Mitchell finished with 22 points, shooting 7-for-19 from the floor. Harden led Cleveland with 24 points and Merrill contributed 16 as the Cavs dropped to 3-2, losing both of their road games thus far.

Both teams are off until Saturday when the Hawks visit the New Orleans Pelicans and the Cavs travel to play the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: Los Hawks se reponen, los Pelicans ganan y Ja Morant no se venga de Memphis: "No quería irme"
articles.standfirst: Triunfos de Atlanta Hawks, New Orleans Pelicans y Memphis Grizzlies en la jornada NBA
articles.summary: Triunfos de Atlanta Hawks, New Orleans Pelicans y Memphis Grizzlies en la jornada NBA
articles.body: Los Atlanta Hawks cortaron su racha de tres derrotas al vencer por 114-111 a los Cleveland Cavaliers, mientras que los New Orleans Pelicans consiguieron su primera victoria de la temporada de la NBA con un triunfo por 132-120 sobre los Sacramento Kings, que continúan sin ganar después de cinco partidos. Los Memphis Grizzlies derrotaron por 124-103 a los Portland Trail Blazers y acabaron con el invicto de su exjugador Ja Morant, en el primer reencuentro del base con la franquicia que le llevó a la NBA. El encuentro en Atlanta comenzó a las 20:00 hora local, una hora después de lo previsto, porque el State Farm Arena había acogido el sexto encuentro de las Finales de la WNBA entre Atlanta Dream y Golden State. Onyeka Okongwu encabezó a Atlanta con 29 puntos, 12 rebotes y 4 triples en 6 intentos, Nickeil Alexander-Walker lo acompañó con 25 puntos y Aaron Wiggins fue fundamental desde el banquillo con 20 unidades y 4 aciertos desde el perímetro. Jalen Johnson contribuyó con 17 puntos, 8 rebotes y 7 asistencias para los locales. James Harden lideró a Cleveland con 24 tantos y Donovan Mitchell agregó 22, aunque convirtió solamente uno de sus 9 triples. Sam Merrill aportó 16 puntos desde el banquillo, insuficientes para evitar que los Cavaliers vieran interrumpida su racha de tres victorias consecutivas. En New Orleans, los Pelicans dejaron atrás cuatro derrotas consecutivas gracias a una actuación grupal encabezada por Zion Williamson y Jeremiah Fears, autores de 22 puntos cada uno. Los locales castigaron las pérdidas de Sacramento y dominaron cerca del aro para imponerse por 132-120. Williamson convirtió 10 de sus 12 lanzamientos y añadió 6 rebotes y 5 robos. Fears completó su aportación con 13 asistencias, 8 rebotes y 4 tapones. Los Kings cerraron el primer cuarto arriba 30-24, pero New Orleans respondió con un total de 78 puntos en los dos períodos siguientes. Así construyó una ventaja de 102-88 antes del último cuarto, suficiente para contener la reacción visitante. Darius Acuff Jr. destacó por Sacramento con 34 puntos y 14 asistencias. De'Andre Hunter y Precious Achiuwa anotaron 24 cada uno, mientras Zach LaVine aportó 21. Domantas Sabonis recogió 15 rebotes y repartió 7 asistencias, pero se quedó en 9 tantos y perdió 7 balones. En un duelo entre equipos invictos los Grizzlies prolongaron su pleno gracias al triple-doble de Cameron Boozer, con 18 puntos, 11 rebotes y 12 asistencias. Isaiah Stewart añadió 18 tantos y Cedric Coward aportó 17. Ja Morant, traspasado a Portland el 29 de junio a cambio de Jerami Grant y Kris Murray, terminó con 14 puntos y 3 asistencias. Deni Avdija encabezó a los locales con 24 tantos, 9 rebotes y 7 asistencias. Elegido por Memphis con el número dos del draft de 2019, Morant fue novato del año y alcanzó su mejor promedio anotador en la temporada 2021-22, con 27,4 puntos, cuando los Grizzlies ganaron 56 partidos y llegaron a las semifinales del Oeste. Las lesiones y dos suspensiones por problemas relacionados con armas de fuego frenaron su progresión. En 2023 recibió sanciones de 8 y 25 partidos, antes de que la reconstrucción del equipo llevara a su salida tras siete temporadas. "No quería irme", reconoció antes del encuentro Morant, aunque aseguró sentirse feliz en Portland y con menos presión.

articles.title: “There’s some freaks in this league”: 6-foot-8 Denver Nuggets forward gives subtle warning to Luka Doncic’s Warriors rival amid rematch hype
articles.summary: Aaron Gordon has a message for Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, and it is not a gentle one.
articles.body: Aaron Gordon has a message for Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, and it is not a gentle one. The Denver Nuggets forward told the first-year player to stay with it because of some monstrous superstars. Of course, he did not name Luka Doncic but it appears to be a subtle hint. Gordon backed the warning with a story of his own, which began as a No. 1 option in Orlando and ended with a title in Denver. The words reach Lendeborg as the Warriors get ready for another night against Luka Doncic and the Lakers. Lendeborg and Doncic already traded words on opening night. Friday brings round two at Chase Center.What did Aaron Gordon tell Yaxel Lendeborg?The 6-foot-8 forward spoke in a conversation shared online, and the message was plain. Showing up with talent does not protect anyone from getting humbled.Gordon used Orlando as the example. He said the idea of being the top option there was not really true. Denver asked for less, a few steps back in role. The result was a championship and a better all-around game today.“As far as, like, your NBA journey, just stay with it. There’s some freaks in this league, you know what I mean? Like real monsters in this league,” Gordon said.Lendeborg got a second piece of advice. Gordon told the rookie to carry the lessons from his mother and from work, since those are the reasons Golden State picked him.The path is different from the one Lendeborg is on. Gordon took a smaller role to win. The rookie is carrying a scoring load the Warriors need.How has Lendeborg played ahead of the Luka Doncic rematch?Through five games, Lendeborg is averaging 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.0 steals. The past three have been stronger, at 27.7 points and 10.0 rebounds a night. Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. is the only other first-year player scoring at a similar rate, and his efficiency is far lower.Doncic has been bigger still. He leads the league at 36.0 points a game through four, with 52 against Utah and 41 against Portland. Soreness kept him out of Wednesday’s win over the Clippers, but Lakers coach JJ Redick does not expect another absence.Opening night set the tone. Lendeborg started the chatter while guarding Doncic, picked up a technical, and the Lakers won. Warriors coach Steve Kerr has said he would rather the rookie ease off, yet he is not trying to change him. Stephen Curry and Draymond Green want the emotion to stay. articles.title: Ja Morant Injured in Revenge Game vs. Grizzlies, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Dame, Cam Boozer
articles.summary: For the first time since being traded to the Portland Trail Blazers, Ja Morant went up against his former team.
articles.body:
For the first time since being traded to the Portland Trail Blazers, Ja Morant went up against his former team.

Unfortunately for him and the Blazers, his revenge game was a loss as the Memphis Grizzlies won 124-103 to improve to 5-0 on the season. The loss was Portland's first of the season.

Morant's night also ended prematurely when he was ruled out in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury.

Morant spent his seven seasons in the NBA with the Grizzlies and became one of the most beloved players in franchise history, but things turned rocky in his final season, and he was eventually traded over the summer.

Morant discussed the matchup earlier this week, calling it "just another basketball game on the schedule."

"Nothing harsh from me for Memphis," he said. "At all."

Harsh feelings or not, Morant would have liked to pick up a win against his former squad.

Deni Avdija has had a strong start to the campaign as he looks to continue establishing himself among the best in the league, and that continued on Thursday despite the loss.

On the Grizzlies' side, standout rookie Cam Boozer, the No. 4 overall pick, picked up the first of likely many triple-doubles in his young career.

The Grizzlies were presumed to be a rebuilding team this year, but after a 5-0 start, that might not be the case. Memphis is one of the youngest teams in the league, but that certainly isn't stopping it from aiming for the playoffs this year.

The Blazers, meanwhile, have also had a strong start to the year despite dropping Thursday's game.

They'll face the Grizzlies again in February, when Morant will have his homecoming game.

articles.title: Trail Blazers' Ja Morant ruled out of loss to Grizzlies with hamstring injury
articles.summary: Morant's 'revenge game' against his former team ended early due to injury, before Memphis got the win to move to 5-0 on the season.
articles.body:
Ja Morant's first meeting with his former team as a Portland Trail Blazer came to an early end, after the guard exited the game with a left hamstring injury.

Halfway through the fourth quarter of Thursday's game against the Memphis Grizzlies, Morant appeared to grab at his left hamstring after a few back-and-forth plays. He went to the bench shortly afterward and had his leg checked out on the sideline.

The 27-year-old point guard was officially ruled out by the team later in the quarter. The severity of the injury is unclear.

Morant was set up for an early meeting with his old team, just four months after the blockbuster trade that sent Morant to Portland . But the Grizzlies got the last laugh in the end, picking up a 124-103 win in Portland's Moda Center.

Prior to leaving with the injury, Morant struggled with shooting but dropped some big highlights in the contest. In one moment late in the second quarter, the guard dropped a floating jumper past Grizzlies guard Cedric Coward; Morant then seemingly mouthed "he food" at the crowd while pointing toward Coward.

Morant finished with 14 points, 2 rebounds and 3 assists in 23 minutes of play.

The game was close at first, with the two teams tied up at halftime, but Memphis started to pull away in the second half to get the win. Cameron Boozer, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft , earned his first triple-double (18 points, 12 rebounds, 12 assists) in the victory, which moves the Grizzlies to 5-0 on the season.

Morant's time with Memphis — from when he was drafted by the team in 2019 until his trade this summer — was often defined by his off-court issues. He was suspended by the team last season after reportedly getting into a verbal spat with head coach Tuomas Iisalo; in 2023, he started the season with a league-enforced 25-game suspension after brandishing a gun in public.

The trade to Portland felt like a chance for the Grizzlies to turn the page on a disappointing era, while also giving Morant a fresh start. Morant's time with the Trail Blazers had seemed positive so far, with the guard leading the team in assists and serving as a complementary scorer to teammates Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard.

articles.title: Kings’ Darius Acuff Jr. joins LeBron James in rare NBA club with fiery stats vs. Pelicans
articles.summary: The Sacramento Kings are still winless through five games into their 2026-27 NBA season, but at least they know they have a special young talent in Darius Ac...
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings are still winless through five games into their 2026-27 NBA season, but at least they know they have a special young talent in Darius Acuff Jr .

The 19-year-old rookie Acuff went off with an impressive individual performance in Thursday night's 132-120 loss at the hands of Zion Williamson and the New Orleans Pelicans at Smoothie King Center in New Orleans.

The former Arkansas Razorbacks star guard produced a game-high 34 points on 13-for-26 shooting from the field, but he also figured in Sacramento's offense a lot beyond just putting up buckets. Acuff dished out 14 assists to lead all players in the contest, while adding six rebounds and a steal in 41 minutes of action.

With his performance, Acuff joined Philadelphia 76ers star and future Basketball Hall of Famer LeBron James in an extremely exclusive all-time NBA club.

Acuff became just the latest (and fourth ever) player to have at least 30 points and 10 assists or more in a game as a teenager in NBA history, according to Cameron Salerno of CBS Sports.

James did it three times, while Stephon Marbury and Luka Doncic are the other two players on the short list.

Acuff wasn't the only Kings player who had a big statistical night wasted in a loss. De'Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa each had 24 points, while Domantas Sabonis had a 15-rebound night go for naught.

Acuff, selected seventh overall by the Kings in the 2026 NBA Draft, has yet to taste a win in the regular season, but he and the Kings will try again on Saturday, when they visit the Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum in Memphis.

articles.title: ‘Doing Irreversible Damage to His Legacy,’ ‘Gotta Hang It Up’ — NBA Fans React As LeBron James Gets Chase-Down Blocked in 76ers-Pacers Clash
articles.summary: LeBron James was chased down and blocked from behind during the Philadelphia 76ers’ matchup against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night. The rejection came...
articles.body:
LeBron James was chased down and blocked from behind during the Philadelphia 76ers' matchup against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night.

The rejection came from a Pacers reserve, and fans wasted little time turning the play into a conversation about the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar's age and whether he should retire.

LeBron James' Viral Moment vs. Pacers Fuels Retirement Talk Among Fans

The four-time MVP went up for a transition layup in the second quarter at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, but Pacers forward Jalen Slawson caught him from behind and erased the shot. Officials initially called a foul before Indiana successfully challenged the ruling. The two spoke after the play.

Slawson, one of Indiana's two-way players, was getting minutes with the Pacers short-handed. He finished with 2 points in 12 minutes.

NBA Central posted the clip with the caption: "LeBron just got blocked on a chase down."

YouTuber and streamer Dom2K responded : "McQueen is fading."

One fan compared the 76ers star's current form to his play in previous seasons: "You can tell he's lost a step even from last year's playoffs against Houston. He got chase down blocked by a bench player in the beginning of the game. LeBron 8 years ago punches that."

Another fan imagined the four-time NBA Finals MVP discussing the moment after his retirement: "This is the play LeBron will reference on Mind The Game podcast when he talks about when he knew it was time to retire."

One reaction suggested this could be his final year: "Might be Bron last season."

Another was more direct : "LeBron's gotta hang it up after getting chased down blocked."

A later response questioned what another season might do to his legacy: "This gotta be LeBron's last season man. Bro out here doing irreversible damage to his legacy."

Philadelphia trailed by 13 entering the fourth quarter after Indiana went on a 17-0 run in the third. Tyrese Maxey scored 17 points in the final period as the 76ers rallied for a 114-109 win.

James contributed to the comeback. He blocked Kelly Oubre Jr. to set up a Maxey fast-break layup, hit a 3-pointer that cut Indiana's lead to 5 points, and found Joel Embiid for a layup and a foul.

The 41-year-old finished with 13 points on 5-for-12 shooting in 33 minutes. He added 5 rebounds, and his 10 assists led the 76ers. He did not commit a turnover and blocked 2 shots, matching Indiana's total for the game.

articles.title: Celtics Announce $200 Million Gift With an Impact Far Beyond Basketball
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics are making a commitment that deserves attention from far beyond their fan base. Boston Children’s Hospital announced a gift of more than $...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics are making a commitment that deserves attention from far beyond their fan base. Boston Children's Hospital announced a gift of more than $200 million from the Celtics ownership group and the team, in association with the Boston Celtics Shamrock Foundation. The donation will support several priorities involving children's care, research and families.

The announcement gives the headline figure a purpose. This is not money attached to a ceremonial presentation. The hospital identified areas the gift will support, including pediatric mental health, nursing education and medical research.

For Celtics fans, that provides a reason to appreciate the organization beyond its basketball results. A championship can bring a city together. A commitment to children's health has the potential to reach families whose concerns have nothing to do with the standings.

Among the priorities is building a pediatric mental health facility and supporting earlier intervention for children experiencing crises. The gift will also help fund research into childhood illnesses and the origins of diseases that affect adults. Those goals extend the announcement beyond one department or one type of treatment.

Additional priorities include advanced training for pediatric nurses, an innovation fund and community programs promoting healthy lifestyles for families. The breadth matters because improving care involves more than a building. It also depends on the people delivering treatment and the ideas that could improve it.

Still, the announcement should not be mistaken for a list of completed projects. Funding creates opportunities for work to advance. The results will emerge through implementation, research and the care patients receive.

Celtics Ownership Emphasizes Children's Futures

Celtics chairman and governor Bill Chisholm connected the contribution to the next generation. His statement described the gift as part of the organization's responsibility beyond competition. The closing line captured that intention.

"We all win when we invest in our children's futures," Chisholm said.

That is an appropriate standard for evaluating the announcement. The amount attracts attention, but its value will depend on what it helps accomplish. Families seeking answers need progress that reaches them, rather than another impressive number.

Boston Children's Hospital CEO Dr. Kevin Churchwell emphasized the human impact. He said the gift's significance would be measured by "the lives it will save." That places the focus where it belongs: on patients and their families.

The Celtics also plan to recognize people connected to the hospital during their October 30 home game. The celebration will include patients, families and staff. It offers supporters an opportunity to see the people behind the announcement.

Basketball will continue to generate arguments about what the Celtics should do next. This commitment offers something different to recognize. Its ambition is helping children build futures that extend well beyond any season.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Shares Troubling Safety Update as WNBA Popularity Brings Unsettling Attention From Stalkers
articles.summary: Over the past year and a half, Sophie Cunningham has risen in popularity within the sports world and beyond. For the Indiana Fever guard, though, this hasn’t...
articles.body:
Over the past year and a half, Sophie Cunningham has risen in popularity within the sports world and beyond. For the Indiana Fever guard, though, this hasn't always been a pleasant experience.

On Wednesday's "This Past Weekend" podcast, Cunningham said that the FBI is keeping tabs on individuals due to concerns that they might be stalking her.

"We do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do. That's the negative side of things that people don't think about. … I have, I think, 20 people that the FBI are watching for me alone."

Cunningham added that she knows one of the individuals suspected of stalking. An avid lover of animals, Cunningham joked that she might have to rename a miniature donkey that she owns, given that this donkey shares a name with a person who was charged with felony stalking .

Aside from Cunningham, there have been other prominent WNBA names who have experienced being followed and getting harassed in recent years. In July 2025, a 55-year-old man pled guilty to charges of stalking and harassing Caitlin Clark. He was subsequently sentenced to two and a half years in prison.

In February, then-Atlanta Falcons rookie James Pearce Jr. was arrested for aggravated stalking and other felony charges after he crashed into the car of his ex-girlfriend Rickea Jackson.

Sophie Cunningham Credits 2024 WNBA Draft Class for Expanding League's Fanbase: "They Had the Audience From College"

In the same podcast appearance, Sophie Cunningham gave props to the college stars who were drafted two years ago for helping the WNBA become more popular.

Cunningham, who was drafted 13th out of Missouri in 2019, said that the 2024 draft class brought more eyeballs to the league.

"That class of Caitlin, Cameron Brink, Hailey Van Lith, Angel (Reese), they just had the platform. They had the eyes. They had the audience from college. They brought it to the W, and now, it's just exploded."

Cunningham went on to hail the WNBA for becoming "so diverse" and inspiring young girls to pursue basketball careers.

articles.title: Boozer shines as Grizzlies top Blazers in battle of NBA unbeatens
articles.summary: The Memphis Grizzlies, fueled by a triple-double from teenager Cameron Boozer, topped the Portland Trail Blazers 124-103 in a battle of NBA unbeatens on Thur...
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies, fueled by a triple-double from teenager Cameron Boozer, topped the Portland Trail Blazers 124-103 in a battle of NBA unbeatens on Thursday, Portland guard Ja Morant's first game against his former team ending with an injury.

Boozer, taken third in June's NBA draft, scored 18 points with 12 rebounds and 12 assists for the Grizzlies.

The game in Portland was billed as Morant's reunion with the Grizzlies, the team that drafted him second overall in 2019. He earned Rookie of the Year honors in 2020 and emerged as a star in his seven-year tenure in Memphis.

He also had a pair of lengthy suspensions and, after multiple injuries limited him to 20 games last season, he was traded in June.

Morant finished with 14 points, two rebounds and three assists before exiting in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury.

Boozer, meanwhile, stole the show, becoming at 19 years and 103 days the second-youngest player in NBA history to post a triple-double, after Josh Giddey in 2022 (19 years, 84 days).

"It's nice," Boozer said. "I'm going to keep going. Season just started, we've got 77 more (games) -- so a lot more to come."

Isaiah Stewart added 18 points off the bench and eight players scored in double figures for the Grizzlies, who improved to 5-0. They and the 5-0 Houston Rockets are the only remaining unbeaten teams.

The New Orleans Pelicans, fueled by a 22-point, 13-assist double-double from Jeremiah Fears, bagged their first win of the season with a 132-120 victory over the Sacramento Kings.

Fears, 20, added eight rebounds, four blocked shots, and two steals, and Zion Williamson scored 22 points for the Pels, who had seven players score in double figures to improve to 1-4.

"We're not off to a great start, but we're changing this thing around for sure," Fears said.

Sacramento's Darius Acuff Jr., the seventh overall pick in the draft, continued his strong rookie season with 34 points and 14 assists -- topping his previous career-high of 33 points set last week against Portland.

De'Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa added 24 points each for the Kings, but Sacramento fell to 0-5. They're one of two remaining winless teams along with the 0-4 Brooklyn Nets.

The Hawks got a much-needed win in Atlanta, taking charge with a 43-point third quarter and holding on for a 114-111 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Onyeka Okongwu scored 29 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 25 points, and Aaron Wiggins added 20 points off the bench for the Hawks, who had lost three straight and grabbed their first home win of the fledgling season.

James Harden scored 24 points for the Cavs, who led by as many as 15 in the first half.

Donovan Mitchell added 22, including a driving layup that pulled Cleveland within 112-111 with 20.6 seconds remaining. Alexander-Walker made a pair of free throws, and Mitchell missed a pair of potential game-tying three-pointers in the waning seconds.

articles.title: 40 años del debut de Fernando Martín en la NBA: el inicio del sueño americano de España
articles.standfirst: El 31 de octubre de 1986 el pionero Fernando Martín se convirtió en el primer español en debutar en la NBA
articles.summary: El 31 de octubre de 1986 el pionero Fernando Martín se convirtió en el primer español en debutar en la NBA
articles.body: El 31 de octubre de 1986 siempre será una fecha de celebración para el baloncesto español. Un día inolvidable cuyo protagonista fue un pionero, visto lo que llegó después. Este sábado se cumplen 40 años del debut de Fernando Martín en la NBA, cuatro décadas del primer español en la mejor liga del mundo. Ataviado con la camiseta de los Portland Trail Blazers, franquicia que después sería la casa de otras leyendas del baloncesto español como Sergio Rodríguez, Rudy Fernández o Víctor Claver, Martín (Madrid, 1962) hizo historia al saltar a la pista del Veterans Memorial Coliseum de Oregón ante los Seattle Supersonics. Fueron poco más de dos minutos, en los que apenas pudo llevar a cabo ninguna acción destacable, pero, sin duda, fue todo un acontecimiento para un país entregado a la pasión futbolera que, desde entonces, empezó a mirar el baloncesto con otros ojos. Como se sabe, el paso de Martín por los Blazers no fue del todo fructífero. En los 80, la liga estadounidense aún no estaba preparada para la apertura total al jugador foráneo. En aquel entonces, el americano gozaba de mayor estatus, y los europeos, especialmente, cargaron durante años con el cliché de ser más débiles a nivel físico. Sólo fue una temporada en la franquicia de Oregon, hasta 1987, pero fue suficiente para que España descubriese por completo los entresijos de la NBA, en una apertura mediática que se prolonga hasta la actualidad. Martín fue elegido en el puesto 38 de la segunda ronda del Draft de 1985 por los New Jersey Nets, con los que prefirió no firmar un contrato no garantizado tras participar en su campus de verano, retrasando así su salto a la liga, que se produciría un verano más tarde con los Blazers. El madrileño nunca contó en Portland con la confianza del técnico Mike Schuler. Allí, compartió vestuario con jugadores de la talla de Clyde Drexler, Walter Berry, Terry Porter o Sam Bowie, que pasaría a la historia como el jugador al que los de Oregon eligieron en 1983 antes que a Michael Jordan. Desencantado ante la falta de minutos, 146 en total repartidos en 24 partidos, Martín regresó al Real Madrid en el verano de 1987, que volvieron a contar con sus servicios tras una difícil negociación con los Blazers. Allí jugaría sus últimas dos temporadas antes de perder la vida en un accidente de tráfico el 3 de diciembre de 1989, con 27 años. 20 años después de su fallecimiento, otro jugador español como Rudy Fernández, que también se convertiría en otro de los iconos del club blanco, homenajeó a Martín mostrando su camiseta en el Concurso de Mates de la NBA en 2009. Antes de emigrar en búsqueda del sueño americano, Martín ya mostró su precocidad en el Estudiantes. Pese a iniciarse en el baloncesto con 15 años, a los 17 ya hizo su debut con el club madrileño en la temporada 1979/1980. Habitual en las categorías inferiores de la selección y tras consolidarse en la rotación estudiantil, el Real Madrid pagó 20 millones de pesetas (120.202 euros), récord de la época, para firmar al joven interior, que parecía cerrado por el Joventut de Badalona. Con los blancos se convirtió en un símbolo. Desde su llegada en 1981 y en pleno apogeo madridista, conquistó cuatro títulos de la Liga ACB (1982, 1984, 1985 y 1986), tres de Copa del Rey (1985,1986 y 1989), dos Recopas (1984 y 1989), una copa Korac (1988) un Mundial de Clubs (1982) y un subcampeonato de la Copa de Europa (1985). En plenos años 80, la capital de España se topó con la 'movida madrileña'. Aquel movimiento cultural, marcado por el desenfreno y la ruptura de la moral tradicional de los años pretéritos, influyó a toda una generación. Trasladado a la pista, Martín también se convirtió en un transgresor. Parte de su éxito llegó al reconvertir la posición de pívot. Con sus 205 centímetros de altura y su porte atlético, era capaz de correr en la cancha como un alero, alejándose de la rigidez de los hombres altos que dominaban la pintura en aquella época. Su espíritu guerrero y tesón bajo los aros le auparon como uno de los grandes héroes del Pabellón de la Ciudad Deportiva del equipo 'merengue'. Con España, bajo el mando de Antonio Díaz-Miguel, y con jugadores como Epi, Juan Antonio Corbalán o Ignacio Solozábal, entre otros, consiguió la plata en el Eurobasket de 1983 y la histórica plata en los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles en 1984. Su popularidad hizo que la empresa Dynamic Software lanzase el videojuego Fernando Martín Basket Master en 1987. De esta forma, Martín volvió a ser pionero, siendo el primer deportista español de élite que cedió sus derechos de imagen para dar nombre a un videojuego. Años más tarde, otras leyendas del deporte nacional como el futbolista Emilio Butragueño, el piloto Carlos Sainz o el boxeador Poli Díaz harían lo mismo. El madrileño también consiguió ser un icono popular por su vida privada. La atracción que generaron sus relaciones personales fue noticia para la prensa del corazón de aquella época, siendo prácticamente la primera figura en España que trascendió más allá del deporte. Martín murió el 3 de diciembre de 1989 en un accidente en la M-30 madrileña cuando se dirigía a presenciar, él estaba lesionado, un partido en el que sus compañeros del Real Madrid se enfrentaban al CAI Zaragoza. El jugador perdió el control de su coche, un Lancia Thema, se saltó la mediana cuando se incorporaba a la M-30 e invadió el carril de sentido contrario impactando contra otro vehículo, conducido por Ricardo Delgado Cascales, quien sobrevivió al accidente con graves heridas. A día de hoy, su mítico dorsal '10' es el único retirado por el Real Madrid a modo de homenaje. EFE

articles.title: El FBI controla a 20 acosadores de la "MAGA Barbie", la voz crítica de las jugadoras de la WNBA
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham asegura que el FBI está vigilando a 20 personas en relación con su seguridad
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham asegura que el FBI está vigilando a 20 personas en relación con su seguridad
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham (Indiana Fever) no se mantiene al margen del debate sobre los equipos de la WNBA que deciden no estar presentes durante el himno nacional de Estados Unidos. La conocida como "MAGA (Make America Great Again) Barbie" habló con el comediante Theo Von, en el podcast 'This Past Weekend', sobre la decisión de las Atlanta Dream y Golden State Valkyries de dejar la pista antes de que sonara 'The Star-Spangled Banner' en las Finales de la WNBA. La controversia ha llegado a los niveles más altos del gobierno de Estados Unidos. El vicepresidente JD Vance arremetió contra la medida, afirmando que los jugadoras no deberían protestar contra las políticas de un político faltando al respeto al país. "¿Sabes con quién estás hablando? Me siento muy orgullosa de mis raíces y estoy orgullosa de ser ciudadana estadounidense. Eso no significa que todos piensen igual", dejó claro la jugadora de las Fever, que tiene familiares que han servido en el ejército, y siempre que tiene la oportunidad de reconocer a los veteranos y a quienes actualmente luchan por el país, les expresa su apoyo y cariño. Sophie Cunningham, que se convertirá en agente libre sin restricciones al finalizar esta temporada, le reveló a Theo Von algo alarmante: ha recibido amenazas y ha sido víctima de acoso. La escudera de Caitlin Clark en las Indiana Fever asegura que el FBI está vigilando a unas 20 personas en relación con su seguridad. Un hombre de 49 años fue detenido en junio y enfrenta cargos graves por acoso e intimidación, además de un cargo menor por hostigamiento. Cunningham, elegida en el puesto número 13 del draft de 2019 por las Phoenix Mercury, tiene planeado jugar esta temporada en el extranjero. "Les aseguro que el 90 % del drama en la WNBA son puras tonterías inventadas. Es perfectamente normal que las mujeres compitan y tengan rivalidades... De eso tratan los deportes", dijo Cunningham sobre las polémicas que la han salpicado en los últimos meses. Cuando Von le preguntó sobre las relaciones sentimentales de las jugadoras, Cunningham aclaró que ella solo sale con hombres y que se mantiene "al margen de todo ese enredo... Simplemente me siento a observar con mis palomitas cómo se desarrollan las cosas". Sophie Cunningham, que fue bautizada como adulta en abril, confesó que su fe cristiana le ayuda a mantener el equilibrio frente a los elogios y las críticas: "No me importan las opiniones de los demás sobre mí, porque no vivo buscando su aprobación". La escolta de 30 años y 1,85 m. desmintió el rumor de que participaría en el programa de telerrealidad 'Love Island' y aseguró que ahora está plenamente dedicada a su fe cristiana.

articles.title: Primera lista de la selección femenina tras el bronce del Mundial
articles.standfirst: España afrontará la primera Ventana de clasificación para el Europeo de 2027 ante República Checa (Oviedo el 10 de noviembre), Bulgaria (Samokov el 14) y Croacia (Porec el 17)
articles.summary: España afrontará la primera Ventana de clasificación para el Europeo de 2027 ante República Checa (Oviedo el 10 de noviembre), Bulgaria (Samokov el 14) y Croacia (Porec el 17)
articles.body: Vuelven las chicas de bronce. La selección femenina, tras el brillante tercer puesto en el Mundial del pasado verano, regresa a la acción para afrontar la primera Ventana FIBA de clasificación para el Eurobasket de 2027. El equipo nacional se concentrará el 7 de noviembre y se medirá a sus tres rivales de grupo: recibirá a República Checa en Oviedo el día 10 (20.30 horas), viajará a Samokov para medirse a Bulgaria el sábado 14 (18.00 h.) y cerrará ante Croacia el día 17 (18.00 h.) en la localidad de Porec. El seleccionador Miguel Méndez ha anunciado este viernes una lista con 14 jugadoras entre las que hay ocho de las medallistas en el Mundial de Berlín. La eterna capitana Alba Torrens comanda una nómina en la que también figuran Elena Buenavida, Raquel Carrera, Maite Cazorla, Paula Ginzo, Mariona Ortiz, Helena Pueyo e Iyana Martín, referente de la selección y que vivirá un partido muy especial jugando en Oviedo, su casa. Junto a ellas, algunas de las jugadoras que ayudaron a preparar el torneo pero fueron descartadas: Txell Alarcón, María Araújo, Aina Ayuso, Irati Etxarri y Andrea Vilaró. La gran novedad es la presencia de Marta Suárez, que ha recalado esta temporada en el Valencia Basket tras formarse en la NCAA y jugar la WNBA. Podía hacer su debut con la selección. Las principales ausencias son las de Awa Fam, María Conde, Alicia Flórez y Megan Gustafson, que estuvieron en el Mundial. “Por primera vez vamos a jugar tres partidos en una misma Ventana de clasificación, en unos 10 días. Podemos hacer una convocatoria diferente en cada partido y por eso de estas 14 no habrá descartes", ha explicado Méndez, que ha aportado por "una lista muy continuista respecto a lo que hemos hecho este verano. Nos faltan varias jugadoras que no podrán estar porque no han dado su disponibilidad por diferentes motivos, pero estoy seguro de que con estas 14 jugadoras volveremos a hacer el mejor equipo posible, que juegue junto, que nos represente a todos, y que sacaremos adelante estos partidos con victorias”. El Eurobasket de 2027 se disputará en Bélgica, Finlandia, Lituania y Suecia. Son 24 las selecciones que luchan por estar en la cita y para ello hay dos Ventanas de clasificación: esta y una segunda entre el 7 al 17 de febrero. Se clasificarán 12 equipos. España está encuadrada en el Gurpo J, junto a República Checa, Bulgaria y Croacia. Los dos primeros del grupo estarán en el Eurobasket, para el que ya tienen plaza los cuatro anfitriones.

articles.title: 2 Bold Trade Ideas to Save Depleted OKC Thunder's Season
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder were one win away from a return trip to the NBA Finals, but the loss of Jalen Williams (hamstring) gave the San Antonio Spurs the edge they needed to win Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder were one win away from a return trip to the NBA Finals, but the loss of Jalen Williams (hamstring) gave the San Antonio Spurs the edge they needed to win Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals.

Now Williams is out for a long time after suffering a devastating dislocated left ankle and broken fibula in Sunday's loss to the LA Clippers. Cason Wallace (shoulder) also went down in that game and is out for months—neither may return this year, regardless of how far the franchise goes in the playoffs.

Are the Thunder still an elite contender? What can they do to restore their shaken depth?

The good news: the team has multiple trade exceptions and enough draft compensation to get a deal or two done. The bad news: the luxury-tax bill.

The Oklahoma City Thunder receive: Herb Jones, $4.9 million trade exception (Thomas Sorber)

The New Orleans Pelicans receive: Thomas Sorber, 2027 first-round pick (second-highest of LA Clippers, top-5 protected Denver Nuggets, and Thunder), 2027 Chicago Bulls second-round pick, $14.9 million trade exception (Herb Jones)

The Oklahoma City Thunder receive: Derrick Jones Jr.

The LA Clippers receive: 2027 first-round pick (highest of Clippers, top-5 protected Denver Nuggets, and Thunder), 2029 Boston Celtics second-round pick, $10.5 million trade exception (Derrick Jones Jr.)

The question for the Thunder is appetite: roster quality vs. tax bill. The team has the roster space, pick flexibility, and trade exceptions to make both deals.

Herb Jones, via the Lu Dort $17.7 million trade exception, is a tremendous switchable defender, comfortable on the point of attack or covering elite-scoring wings. His shooting is inconsistent, but he peaked at 41.8 percent from three-point range in 2023-24. He'd benefit from open looks on a strong squad like the Thunder's.

Derrick Jones Jr. fits within the Isaiah Joe $11.3 million trade exception. If he keeps shooting 53.8 percent from three, the Clippers won't deal him—hot start aside, he should eventually settle near 36 percent. He's another active, versatile wing defender. He's a bouncy athlete who reached the NBA Finals with the Dallas Mavericks.

The Thunder give up two first-rounders in 2027, expendable seconds, and Sorber. The team projects to have a nearly full roster under contract next season; Sorber's importance to Oklahoma City may be marginalized by the addition of Aday Mara.

The team may not be able to replace Williams' scoring and playmaking, but Ajay Mitchell filled that role well last year. The two incoming defenders help offset the loss of Wallace (and Williams) on defense, giving the Thunder the depth needed to resume their championship pursuit.

The franchise may balk at the financial repercussions of the two deals. The Thunder are currently projected at just under $20 million in luxury-tax penalties. After both trades, that jumps to almost $119 million. Oklahoma City also ventures above the second apron but can navigate back under next season. Frozen draft picks only lock in when a team stays above the second apron for multiple seasons.

A compromise could be one of the two, with Sorber routed instead to the Clippers in the Derrick Jones Jr. version for nearly $41 million in penalties, under the second apron.

Herb Jones alone puts the Thunder over the second apron with a $62 million tax bill. He is also a significant commitment, with $67.6 million due over the next three seasons (final year is a player option), unlike Jones Jr., who is on an expiring contract.

Blockbuster Trade to Fix Heat's Bam Issue💡

The Pelicans are in transition, with new leadership building around younger players like Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. That's led to a significant decrease in minutes, with Jones coming off the bench at 17 minutes per game—after starting for almost his entire career with the team.

That's not ideal for Jones and the team, given his contract length. New Orleans swaps him out for what will likely be the Denver Nuggets' first-round pick—whichever is the second-highest among the Clippers, Thunder, and Nuggets.

The Pelicans also get a look at Sorber, who hasn't had much chance to play yet because of injuries, along with what should be a high second-rounder from the Bulls. That's a rich haul for Jones.

New Orleans would acquire Sorber via its Jordan Hawkins trade exception, allowing the franchise to create a new one for Jones' full 2026-27 salary.

The Clippers are also navigating an odd transition from the Kawhi Leonard era to what comes next. The franchise is competitive for now, but its goal isn't as much a deep playoff run as setting up for the future.

Jones Jr. is one of many players on the team in the final year of his contract. None of the veterans have a deal beyond 2027-28. The Clippers could have significant cap room next summer or hold it for massive space in 2028.

Long-term commitments seem off the table; with that in mind, getting a first-rounder back from the Thunder for Jones Jr. is a win. The Clippers still owe Oklahoma City a 2027 swap from the 2023 James Harden acquisition.

If the Thunder finish ahead of the Nuggets, followed by the Clippers, LA would get its own selection back, plus Oklahoma City's selection (which it could then swap with the Toronto Raptors). It's tricky, but the Clippers are looking to replenish their pick stock after forfeiting several following the Leonard investigation.

LA also adds a second-round pick and the trade exception for Jones Jr.'s full salary.
