articles.summary: We're a week and change into the 2026-27 NBA season, and our expectations have been completely upended by the injury bug.
articles.body:
We're a week and change into the 2026-27 NBA season, and our expectations have been completely upended by the injury bug.

Since the campaign began, we've learned that the following players will miss extended time:

Kristaps Porziņģis (possibly out for the season, possibly retiring)

Paolo Banchero (high ankle sprain, 4-6 weeks)

Jalen Suggs (bone bruise, at least two weeks)

Jalen Williams (dislocated ankle and broken fibula, POTS)

Cason Wallace (torn labrum, possibly out for the season)

Kawhi Leonard (swelling in his knee, out for weeks)

Anthony Edwards (arthroscopic knee surgery, up to two months)

Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring strain, at least two weeks)

Somehow, that list isn't even exhaustive.

The avalanche of ailments will obviously impact this week's rankings, but our typical criteria will still control.

Based on team and individual numbers, recent performance, championship chances and plenty of subjectivity, here's how the entire league stacks up right now.

ATL | BKN | BOS | CHA | CHI | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GSW | HOU | IND | LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN | NOP | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX | POR | SAC | SAS | TOR | UTA | WAS

It's hard to overstate (1) how bad the Sacramento Kings are, and (2) how bad Darius Acuff's scoring efficiency was through their first four games.

Acuff, remarkably, was getting a whopping 23.3 shots up per game and averaging just 21.5 points in those opening contests. Plenty of the attempts crossed the line between confident and maddening.

But clearly, there's also plenty of talent there. Acuff was doing a good job of getting where he wanted on the floor. And sure, a lot of those forays ended with shots that probably should've been passes. But you knew the shots would fall one of these nights, and that's exactly what happened Thursday.

In the Kings' fifth loss in five games, Acuff had 34 points, 14 assists, six rebounds and a steal. Most importantly, he was plus-three.

So, while the losses will keep adding up for the Kings, Acuff is absolutely providing some reason for optimism.

Michael Porter Jr. (22.8 points with a 40.5 three-point percentage) and Julius Randle (22.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 5.8 assists) have been their typically productive selves (at least on offense), but the young core isn't doing enough to compete night to night.

Among the 10 Brooklyn Nets who've played at least 50 minutes, only 28-year-old MPJ and 29-year-old Moritz Wagner have above-average box plus/minuses . And that doesn't really capture the ineffectiveness of Egor Dëmin, Noah Clowney, Day'Ron Sharpe, Nolan Traoré and Mikel Brown, who are all below replacement level.

Unless one or two of the up-and-comers take huge steps forward over the course of the season, it won't matter how good Porter and Randle are. The new " relegation zone " is in play for Brooklyn.

The Milwaukee Bucks' first season in the post-Giannis Antetokounmpo era has, as expected, included plenty of losing. But that doesn't mean Bucks fans don't have something to look forward to.

Tyler Herro is only 26, and he's averaging 23.4 points and 4.6 assists. Jaime Jaquez is 25 and averaging 17.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.6 assists.

And several other members of the young core, including Kel'el Ware (11.8 points and 8.4 rebounds in 18.8 minutes), Ryan Rollins (11.6 points), Kasparas Jakučionis (9.0 points and 4.2 assists in 22.7 minutes) and Brayden Burries (7.8 points in 14.9 minutes), have already shown flashes of real upside.

Milwaukee almost certainly isn't going to contend for a play-in spot this season, but it could do so within a year or two.

Grading Every Team After Wild First Week 🔠

The Chicago Bulls look like they could spend the season in the running for a spot in the new, so-called relegation zone, but that doesn't mean they're devoid of hope.

His jump shot looks like it'll need a little more time than the summer league and preseason suggested, but Caleb Wilson is moving like a wing and scoring with confidence in every Bulls outing.

And despite being years away from understanding the nuances of the NBA game, Wilson is averaging 20.8 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.4 blocks.

The Phoenix Suns may have miscalculated how important Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale were to the team's defensive identity and outside shooting in 2025-26.

The player they replaced them with, Miles Bridges, doesn't look capable of being a bona fide second star. Devin Booker appears to be carrying a heavier burden on offense. And Phoenix's lone win came against the injury-ravaged Golden State Warriors.

Barring some unexpected and rapid progression from younger players such as Jalen Green, Oso Ighodaro, Khaman Maluach or Ryan Dunn, it's hard to imagine the Suns recreating last season's surprise success.

The Los Angeles Clippers deserve a little credit for emerging from an offseason about as chaotic as one could get and being better than a total walkover.

The Clippers are around the middle of the pack in net rating, and their 2026 top-five pick, Keaton Wagler, is already showing signs of being a high-end, moneyball scorer.

Wagler is shooting a seemingly impossible 20.0 percent on twos, but he's at 39.1 percent from deep, is averaging 7.8 free-throw attempts in just 26.5 minutes and is second on the team in scoring at 15.0 points per game.

The New Orleans Pelicans are better than their record suggests.

That may sound silly to say of a 1-4 team that had 47 total wins over the two previous seasons, but New Orleans has individual talents (like Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III) and has been within striking distance for most of three of their four losses.

They just aren't able to effectively close right now. That's more of a leadership issue than a talent deficit.

With Jusuf Nurkić still sidelined with a foot injury, Lauri Markkanen day-to-day with a wrist sprain and Jaren Jackson out for at least six weeks with a torn MCL, it'll be up to the young core to try to live up to lofty preseason expectations (at least for the immediate future).

And while Keyonte George (24.4 points, 6.8 assists and a 41.2 three-point percentage) has been good and others have shown flashes, it looks like the time without the vets could be rough.

Rookie Darryn Peterson is barely averaging more points (12.8) than field-goal attempts (12.6). Ace Bailey is shooting 32.0 percent from three. Isaiah Collier has yet to hit a three. And Kyle Filipowski can barely get off the bench.

Few teams have been as well acquainted with injuries as the Orlando Magic over the last few years. And the bug started biting early in 2026-27.

Just this week, the Magic lost Paolo Banchero for 4-6 weeks with an ankle injury. And, as if that wasn't bad enough, just two days later, Jalen Suggs suffered a bone bruise on his knee that will keep him out for at least the next two weeks.

Now down two starters, Orlando is suddenly and woefully short on playmaking. Not having Suggs means the defense is in trouble, too.

And with games against the Toronto Raptors (in Toronto), Boston Celtics and Washington Wizards coming up, the Magic could easily be 1-6 before starting a four-game Western Conference road trip.

The Miami Heat finally got off the schneid with a win over the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday, but it looks like the adjustment period for this team could be tougher than anticipated.

Miami lost its first four games. The fit with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on offense looks, to put it mildly, crowded. Adebayo had 24 on Wednesday, but he's only averaging 12.8 for the season. And as a team, the Heat are barely making over 30 percent of their three-point attempts.

If that last number starts to come up, plenty of other things could fall into place. But starting games with two high-volume scorers who don't command a ton of respect outside the three-point line could make it tough to find a consistent offense.

An 0-3 start had NBA analysts and Golden State Warriors fans in "sky is falling" mode, but they ended this week by blowing out the Denver Nuggets and riding a 44-point outing from Stephen Curry to another victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves (both wins were on the road).

And while Kristaps Porziņģis' health and trade prospects, the injury-related absences of Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody, and Draymond Green looking very much like a player entering his late-30s are all real concerns, Golden State's rookie might already be good enough to keep the Warriors in play-in range until Butler returns.

Yaxel Lendeborg is averaging 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.2 threes. The Warriors are routinely running offense through him. And he and Curry already look like one of the more dynamic inside-out combos in the NBA.

With averages of 21.8 points and 9.5 assists, Tyrese Haliburton has looked very much like the player he was prior to his Achilles injury, but his return hit a speed bump this week.

Haliburton will be out for at least the next two weeks with a hamstring strain, and it'll be tough for the Indiana Pacers to avoid looking like they did last season without him.

It's early, but Indiana is minus-4.4 points per 100 possessions when Haliburton is off the floor.

After missing the first four games with an ankle injury, AJ Dybantsa made his long-awaited NBA debut on Wednesday.

And though the Washington Wizards fell to the Cleveland Cavaliers, Dybantsa's appearance offered plenty of reason for optimism.

He was his team's leading scorer with 19 points. He got there with just 12 field-goal attempts (eight of which were made). He made a three. And he looked like a polished scorer who'd been in the league for years, rather than a 19-year-old playing in his first regular-season game.

At some point, it'll be nice to see some more contributions around the box score (he only had two rebounds and two assists). But on balance, it was undoubtedly a successful first night out.

We haven't seen the Charlotte Hornets anywhere near their complete form.

Kon Knueppel and Coby White still haven't made their season debuts, and that means more minutes and bigger roles for players like Grayson Allen and Dennis Schröder.

Both have been solid filling in and will be even more dangerous spending more time against second units once Knueppel and White are back.

But the biggest reason the Hornets are above .500 while missing two starters is very clearly Brandon Miller. The fourth-year wing is embracing his run as an alpha, averaging 25.6 points and taking 11 triples a game.

The Denver Nuggets are off to a rough start.

One starter (Cameron Johnson) and two potential rotation players (Julian Strawther and Alpha Diallo) are already hurt. Their two wins are against the 1-4 New Orleans Pelicans. One of their losses was a blowout in Denver at the hands of the injury-ravaged Golden State Warriors. And the biggest story of their season so far is Nikola Jokić's chastisement of home fans for booing the team.

On the bright side, one of their best players in this young season is second-round rookie Trevon Brazile, whose contributions feel like found money.

The 6'10" Brazile already looks like the most explosive vertical athlete on the Nuggets, plays with the kind of energy this team has now lacked for years and has already stepped into the starting lineup in the wake of all the injuries.

Five of the Atlanta Hawks' first six games came against teams widely expected to make the playoffs, so the 3-3 start is encouraging, especially after closing the week with a win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

New pickup Aaron Wiggins is offering reason for hope, too.

While Nickeil Alexander-Walker (20.5 points and 3.7 threes, with a 40.0 three-point percentage) and Jalen Johnson (19.0 points, 9.3 rebounds and 8.5 assists) have seemingly picked up right where they left off last season, Wiggins has added length and scoring spark off the bench that could prove crucial.

After dropping 20 points in Thursday's win over Cleveland, Wiggins is now averaging 15.5 points in just 26.0 minutes per game.

The Minnesota Timberwolves' bet on LaMelo Ball is about to be tested.

They looked like a title contender in their first few games of the season, thanks to MVP-like production (33.3 points, 4.5 threes, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals) from Anthony Edwards, but he is going to miss up to two months while recovering from arthroscopic knee surgery.

Without him, Ball is going to have to do more as a scorer. The 40.0 percent he's shooting from the field won't be good enough. He'll need to take better care of the ball. Right now, he's averaging 3.8 turnovers.

Yes, others will have to step up too. And Jaden McDaniels, Terrence Shannon Jr. and Jonathan Kuminga are all capable of providing a little more. But the heavy lifting will have to be done by Ball.

Cooper Flagg's apparent ascension to superstardom is happening much faster than even the most optimistic fans could've imagined.

Still a couple months shy of his 20th birthday, he is getting wherever he wants on the floor, scoring inside and from mid-range and putting up All-NBA numbers through his first four games of the season.

Flagg is at 25.3 points, 6.8 assists, 5.3 rebounds, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks. And here's the kicker. He's doing all that in 30.8 minutes.

His outside shot still isn't falling consistently, but that'll come. And in the meantime, he can keep kicking out of drives to reliable shooters like Kyrie Irving.

The Portland Trail Blazers were on the wrong end of a blowout against the Memphis Grizzlies on Thursday, but early returns on the Ja Morant-Damian Lillard pairing (and how it works with Deni Avdija) have been good.

The worst raw plus-minus between the three of them is Lillard's plus-30, and the threat of his shooting is making the floor feel much more open for Morant and Avdija's drives. Those two, meanwhile, are dragging defenses toward the rim and giving Lillard and the rest of Portland's shooters more time outside.

All of the above will be tested a bit more than it has so far during an upcoming four-game Western Conference road trip, but we at least have a little proof of concept with the team's most important players.

The Memphis Grizzlies were sort of the hipsters' pick to exceed expectations this season. But after a 5-0 start led by Ty Jerome, rookie Cameron Boozer and a well-rounded supporting cast, that take is about as mainstream as it gets now.

Jerome, a 29-year-old guard who spent the beginning of his career on the NBA fringes and averaged 9.3 points in his first seven seasons, put up 34.7 points and 5.7 assists over his first three games.

And while he's had a hard time getting his shot to fall, Boozer's impact in every other category has been obvious. That was true even before he registered his first career triple-double in Thursday's win over the Portland Trail Blazers.

Memphis is huge and skilled, and it shares the ball. Much of the rotation is made up of still-developing players. This isn't just a flash in the pan.

Swelling in his knee has already forced Kawhi Leonard to the sidelines, and it looks like he'll be out for weeks.

But in the two games Kawhi played, he shot just 32.4 percent from the field. And the team's net rating has actually been better without him, thanks to a suffocating defense led by Scottie Barnes.

Barnes has also struggled to hit shots, but he's averaging 5.0 defensive rebounds, 2.3 steals and 1.3 blocks.

The Cleveland Cavaliers' first five games were bookended by losses, but both of those were on the road and against teams that will likely be in the playoffs (the Philadelphia 76ers and Atlanta Hawks).

In between, Cleveland looked capable of 50 wins again. And some subtle development from Evan Mobley is a key reason why.

Mobley has streamlined his game. He's making quick decisions. His catch-and-shoot jump shooting is suddenly a real weapon. And through this early portion of the season, he's averaging 18.2 points, 8.8 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.2 blocks, while shooting 57.1 percent from deep.

With Jalen Duren out for at least the next couple weeks with a hamstring strain, the Detroit Pistons' frontcourt depth will be tested.

But through five games, their defense looks stout and the bigs who'll have to fill in for Duren have the advantage of playing with Cade Cunningham.

With their All-NBA playmaker leading, Paul Reed is averaging 14.2 points and 7.6 rebounds, while John Collins is adding 10.2 points and shooting 41.2 percent from deep.

The New York Knicks opened their 2026-27 campaign with three straight losses, but they look like they're getting right now.

New York beat a hot Detroit Pistons team on Tuesday and then dropped 133 points on the second night of a back-to-back on Wednesday.

In their last contest, Jalen Brunson had 38, bringing his total for 35-point games as a Knick to 67 . He trails only Patrick Ewing in that category, and New York is 45-22 when he hits that benchmark.

The Oklahoma City Thunder are 4-1, but the first week and change of their season couldn't have been much more devastating.

In just their third game of the season, Jalen Williams suffered a gruesome leg injury that was later diagnosed as a dislocated ankle and fractured fibula. In the same contest, Cason Wallace was lost to a torn labrum.

Both could miss the entire season, and now Chet Holmgren and Alex Caruso are out too.

Depth has been a calling card for the Thunder for years, but surviving the long-term loss of two starters will be their biggest test of this era.

He sat out Wednesday's win over the Los Angeles Clippers, and availability is often a question (he's averaged under 65 games per season for his career), but Luka Dončić is off to the races in what could be his first MVP campaign.

His Los Angeles Lakers are 4-1 and have the third-best offense in the league. And after dropping 52 in his last outing, he is putting up an absurd 36.0 points, 8.3 assists and 5.3 threes per game.

There are still serious concerns about L.A.'s defense, but it can win shootouts against anyone. And if the Lakers get to a mid-50s win total while Dončić is putting up numbers anything like the ones above, he could crash the party dominated by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokić over the last couple seasons.

The San Antonio Spurs lost their first two games of the season, but they've now rattled off three straight and their star-studded trio is starting to jell.

Now a fixture in the starting lineup, Dylan Harper is averaging 17.2 points and 4.6 assists, while Stephon Castle is at 17.4 points and 5.4 assists.

And the extra playmaking in that first five is opening up plenty of scoring opportunities for Victor Wembanyama, who's off to an MVP-caliber start with averages of 25.0 points, 11.4 rebounds, 3.8 blocks, 2.8 assists and 1.4 steals.

All three young stars need to shoot better. And the team's offensive numbers will rise if or when that happens. But the early returns for these three are strong.

The Philadelphia 76ers entered the season with plenty of fanfare thanks to the star power they'd acquired over the offseason. Those stars built their reputations primarily on the offensive end.

With Jaylen Brown and LeBron James joining Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe, Philadelphia was supposed to have as much firepower as anyone, but that's not how the team is winning games right now.

Embiid, James, Brown and Edgecombe are shooting a combined 42.1 percent from the field, and the Sixers have a bottom-five offense.

So, how are they winning? Philly is stifling opponents on the other end, particularly when Brown and Embiid are on the floor . And if the 76ers maintain their level of play on that end of the floor while getting more shots to fall on the other, they could quickly become a nightmare for the rest of the league.

The Boston Celtics surrendered a big lead (and eventually lost) against the Detroit Pistons on opening night, but they've rattled off three straight wins since then and now have a top-10 offense .

And more important than the wins and losses, at least at this point in the season, is the fact that Jayson Tatum looks more like his pre-injury self than he did at any point last season.

Tatum's three-pointers aren't consistently falling (he's at 24.1 percent from deep), but he's averaging 28.0 points and 8.0 assists while covering multiple positions on the other end.

The Houston Rockets have charged hard enough out of the gate to change our preseason notions on the Western Conference. And that would have been true with or without the devastating injuries to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Led by Alperen Şengün (24.5 points, 9.0 rebounds and 7.0 assists), Houston has seven players averaging double figures (and Bogdan Bogdanović not far behind at 8.0). They have loads of length and defensive tenacity. And they're third in the league in three-point percentage right now.

There will be tougher stretches of the schedule, but San Antonio, Dallas and Atlanta (twice) are all quality wins. And it's not too early to declare the Rockets bona fide contenders.

articles.title: Ranking the NBA's 10 Best Current Player Beefs
articles.summary: For a few years there, the NBA's biggest stars got along so well it was almost uncomfortable to watch. Thanks to AAU circuits, shoe company camps and brand collaborations, players understand everything is content. Collaboration is key. So friendships were formed from training together every August. No wonder Generation Z players hugged after playoff eliminations like the series had been a group project.
articles.body:
For a few years there, the NBA's biggest stars got along so well it was almost uncomfortable to watch. Thanks to AAU circuits, shoe company camps and brand collaborations, players understand everything is content. Collaboration is key. So friendships were formed from training together every August. No wonder Generation Z players hugged after playoff eliminations like the series had been a group project.

But this season, things have gotten chippy. Within a week of the 2026-27 opener, Kalshi built Dillon Brooks a gadget that mutes LeBron James . Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg guarded Luka Doncic in his NBA debut and told reporters afterward that Doncic no longer had his respect.

Jaylen Brown went into Bleacher Report's Instagram comments to accuse Jayson Tatum of capping about the trade that sent Brown to Philadelphia with a blue hat emoji . The Thunder and Spurs, whose West finals went seven games , just needed one night to start scuffling again .

The beef is back, so we ranked it. Every feud on this list had to clear two bars to get here.

First, it had to be personal. That means two players going at each other—or, in one case, a player and his own locker room. Team rivalries alone don't qualify, and neither do owners. Kevin Durant spent a weekend this month trading shots online with Suns owner Mat Ishbia, and it missed the cut mostly because Ishbia has never had to guard him.

The feud also needed a pulse. Both players have to be active, and neither side can have called a public truce. Jayson Tatum insists there's no beef with Brown. Brown's emoji kept them on the list.

From there, we prioritized how recently a feud boiled over and how ugly it got. A suspension or a flagrant foul pushed it higher. Obviously, Game 7 means more than a regular-season scrum.

This one got physical when Green put Gobert in a chokehold during a Warriors-Timberwolves game on Nov. 14, 2023. The NBA quickly suspended him five games. Gobert called it " clown behavior ." When reporters asked Green about Gobert's comments after the suspension, he was silent...for a whole 16 seconds.

Before any of that, Green called Gobert "soft " on his podcast. When the teams met in the 2025 playoffs, a Warriors staffer rebounded for Green at shootaround in a Gobert jersey. Green later told Fred VanVleet's podcast that he didn't realize how long he held on during the chokehold. He's now the outspoken locker room mentor to a rookie who spent his debut jawing at Luka Doncic, and that rookie shows up later at No. 5.

Green and Gobert haven't had a serious incident since the 2025 playoffs, so they're ranked at the bottom.

In Game 3 of their 2024 first-round series, Embiid grabbed Robinson's leg from the floor and pulled him down. Officials gave him only a flagrant-1.

Asked about the foul afterward, then-Knicks coach Tom Thibodeau answered, "which one?"

Robinson left that night in a walking boot . Embiid said he was trying to keep Robinson from landing on him , citing his own knee history. A year later, Robinson liked a social media post about Embiid's career ending.

Before the teams met again in May, a reporter asked Robinson whether Embiid is a dirty player , and he downplayed the question. In response, New York swept that series. Embiid became public-enemy number one for Knicks fans, cementing his legacy as a dirty, flopping player. But Robinson got his lick back when he posterized Embiid in the Eastern Conference Semifinals on the way to a chip.

Robinson's dunk on Embiid was sweet revenge for Knicks fans, who made quick work of the image on merch across social media.

Robinson then left the champions for a three-year, $47.4 million deal with the Celtics. The 76ers eliminated Boston from the 2026 playoffs with a Game 7 win at TD Garden, and the two teams share a division.

The worst of this beef happened in 2024, and since this list favors recent incidents, it drops to ninth.

8. Kevin Durant vs. His Rockets Teammates

During the February All-Star break, messages from an alleged burner account called @gethigher77 leaked online , criticizing Rockets players Alperen Sengun and Jabari Smith Jr. along with Durant's former Warriors teammates. Durant told reporters he wasn't there to get into " Twitter nonsense " and that his teammates knew what it was. Team sources told ESPN the Rockets took it seriously internally, and Durant talked it through with teammates after the break. ESPN also reported it's unclear whether Durant ever told his teammates if the account was his.

Durant played one game in Houston's six-game first-round loss to the Lakers, and the young core won two elimination games without him.

ESPN reported that Durant's moodiness began to wear on younger players once Fred VanVleet and Steven Adams were out of the locker room. This summer he worked out with Orlando's Paolo Banchero instead of his Rockets teammates, and Kendrick Perkins called him out for it.

Rockets general manager Rafael Stone has defended him publicly .

No Rockets player has criticized Durant on the record, and most of what's public comes from leaks and ESPN's reporting, so the ambiguity keeps it eighth.

The Warriors started Lendeborg in his debut and had him guard Doncic for much of the game. Afterward the rookie said he'd " lost all respect " for Doncic because of the way he begs for calls.

Lendeborg held him to 1-of-6 shooting as the primary defender. Doncic answered with a 48-foot bank shot at the halftime buzzer and pointed at him. The Lakers won 127-105, and Doncic scored 28 in three quarters.

Green backed the rookie and said a player who starts talking should keep going until he can't.

Doncic drew 16 technicals and a one-game suspension last season, and he says he's working on not talking back.

The teams meet again Friday in San Francisco.

It's one game old (for now), so stays at seven.

The Knicks signed Brunson in the summer of 2022 and tried to trade for Mitchell that same summer before he landed in Cleveland. The league treated them as the East's marquee matchup last season and scheduled Knicks-Cavs for opening night and Christmas.

Game 1 of the East finals ended with the Knicks erasing a 22-point fourth-quarter deficit and winning in overtime, led by Brunson's 38.

New York finished the sweep in Cleveland, and Brunson won series MVP in a unanimous vote .

Mitchell averaged 27.3 points , more than Brunson's 25.5, and still lost in four. Afterward he said Cleveland's core would stay intact. (LOL.)

The Knicks swept the last series, and that one-sided result keeps this at No. 6.

The Suns drafted Deandre Ayton with the first overall pick in the 2018 draft and passed on Doncic. In their 2022 playoff series, Booker mocked Doncic's flopping , and Doncic's Mavericks sent Phoenix home. After a 2023 dustup, Doncic told reporters, " Next time, don't wait until there's three seconds left to talk ."

Booker trolled the Mavericks on social media after they traded Doncic, and the trade put the two stars in the same division. In his first game against Phoenix as a Laker, Doncic talked trash at the Suns through a 107-96 win. He has said trash talk gets him going .

Plus, Doncic's classic smile while standing next to Booker entered NBA meme hall-of-fame.

A playoff drought between them since 2022, plus Doncic being traded to Los Angeles, holds this one at fifth.

Like Jay-Z said, "It was all good, just a week ago."

Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia in July for Paul George and draft picks. In his YouTube series, Tatum said he was " just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world ," and he described the Celtics coach who broke the news handing him a towel to put over his face. Brown had felt underappreciated since it came out that Boston included him in talks for Giannis Antetokounmpo. On a Twitch stream, he said he was excited for what comes next despite the " lack of respect " from his old team.

When Bleacher Report posted Tatum's clip on Instagram, Brown commented with a 🧢 emoji. Tatum spent most of his postgame news conference after a 36-point game against the Knicks answering questions about it. He said he called and texted Brown the day of the trade.

Philadelphia eliminated Boston in Game 7 at TD Garden in May, after the Celtics blew a 3-1 series lead. Brown played for Boston in that series and now plays for the team that knocked it out.

Tatum and Brown have only sniped through the media so far, and that keeps them out of the top three.

We're entering historic beef territory now. The Warriors suspended Green one game in November 2018 after an argument with Durant during a loss to the Clippers carried into the locker room. Green later said he lost Durant's trust. Durant left Golden State after that season and told The Wall Street Journal he never truly felt like one of the guys there.

When screenshots from the alleged burner surfaced in February, Green said on his podcast that Durant needed to address them publicly. He joked that walking back into practice would feel like a "Key & Peele" sketch. In August, after Durant said this year's 76ers look more dominant on paper than the 2017-18 Warriors, Green posted on Threads, " Slim thought he was on his burner? "

It ranks top three because the history goes back to the 2018 suspension and Green was still taking public shots at Durant in August.

Everything started in 2021, when James hit shots over Brooks and taunted him as too small. Brooks answered during their 2023 playoff series by calling James old , then got ejected from Game 3 for hitting him in the groin . James has mostly brushed him off.

Brooks set the internet on fire when he showed up to Game 4 of the Lakers and Oklahoma City Thunder playoff series, iced out in all black, laughing like a supervillain in the stands.

This month Brooks starred in a Kalshi commercial for the King Blocker 9000, a mock device that mutes any mention of James. Kalshi is giving away 23 of them .

James signed with rival Polymarket in September in a deal reportedly worth about $15 million a year, so each man now has a prediction market in his corner.

Brooks also sat behind the basket at a Lakers playoff game against Oklahoma City last spring. Some fans took it as a troll.

He's already in another feud this season, after John Collins grabbed him by the throat in the preseason opener.

Five years of history and dueling prediction-market deals put it second.

Wembanyama picked out Holmgren as his rival years before either reached the NBA.

Last December, he waved off the idea anyway, saying, "There's no comparison between us ." Holmgren finished second to him in the 2024 Rookie of the Year race, and then second again in April when Wembanyama became the first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year .

Less than three minutes into Game 7 of the West finals, Wembanyama dunked over Holmgren's outstretched arm . Holmgren attempted two shots all game. He averaged 10.7 points in the series after scoring 17.1 a game in the regular season. San Antonio ended Oklahoma City's title defense on the Thunder's home floor.

The schedule sent the Thunder back to San Antonio for the Oct. 20 opener. A De'Aaron Fox foul on Holmgren set off a scuffle , and Jalen Williams and Jaylin Williams ran in to defend him. B/R's video makes clear the tension from the West Finals is still there.

It's No. 1 because they just met in a Game 7 and both should contend in the West for years.

articles.title: Doug Christie's Kings Hot Seat Updated in New NBA Rumors amid 0-5 Start
articles.summary: Despite a disastrous 0-5 start with the worst net rating in the Western Conference, the Sacramento Kings are not looking to make a change at head coach.
articles.body:
Despite a disastrous 0-5 start with the worst net rating in the Western Conference, the Sacramento Kings are not looking to make a change at head coach.

Per The Athletic's Sam Amick , there is a belief within the Kings' front office that Doug Christie "deserves a fair chance to be evaluated" given the roster he is currently operating with is shorthanded due to key injuries.

Amick added things could end up changing if the Kings continue to lose at the rate they have been, but "development — both his and that of key young players — is considered the most important aspect of his duties."

Christie's job status was a talking point at the end of last season before the Kings announced they were bringing him back.

He is in the final guaranteed year of his current contract with the Kings holding a team option for 2027-28, so it wouldn't cost them anything to let him play out this season before deciding on his future.

The Kings hired Christie on an interim basis midway through the 2024-25 season after Mike Brown was fired. He put together a 27-24 record in 51 games following his promotion to have the interim tag removed.

Since the start of the 2025-26 season, though, Christie has led the Kings to a 22-65 record. The Washington Wizards, Brooklyn Nets and Indiana Pacers are the only teams with a worse record during that stretch.

Injuries have contributed to some of Sacramento's struggles to start this season. Ben Simmons was expected to play a role off the bench after a solid preseason, but he tore his Achilles in practice three days before the regular-season opener.

Maxime Raynaud has yet to play after injuring his knee in a preseason game against the Golden State Warriors on Oct. 10. Keegan Murray will miss at least another week recovering from an ankle injury.

One positive for the Kings is Darius Acuff Jr. looks like the player they hoped for when he was selected with the No. 7 pick in the 2026 draft. He put up a historic stat line with 34 points, 14 assists and one steal against the New Orleans Pelicans on Thursday night.

The Kings and Nets are the lone winless teams in the NBA at this point, but Sacramento has played one more game to be the only 0-5 club.

Christie and the Kings will go for their first win of the season on Saturday against the Memphis Grizzlies at FedEx Forum.

articles.title: Doble palo al Real Madrid en su mejor momento: lesiones de Jantunen y Maledon
articles.standfirst: Se confirma que el ala-pívot finlandés sufre una rotura completa de la fascia plantar del pie izquierdo y el base francés se hizo un esguince en la rodilla derecha
articles.summary: Las bajas del finlandés, Deck y Garuba, la dolencia de Nick Smith Jr., la lenta adaptación de Shulga y Sarr y los pocos minutos de Llull reducen la rotación
articles.body: Malísimas noticias para un Real Madrid que está lanzado en cuanto a juego y resultados. Dentro de la racha que viven de 10 victorias consecutivas, los blancos se han topado con dos serios contratiempos: lesiones de Mikael Jantunen y Theo Maledon. Los problemas físicos empiezan a ser un drama. El primero sufre una rotura completa en la fascia plantar del pie izquierdo y estará de baja por un tiempo indefinido. El habitual "pendiente de evolución" puede leerse en el comunicado médico emitido por el club blanco. Y en este caso conviene recalcarlo porque se trata de un tipo de lesión muy compleja con posibilidad de recaída y pasos atrás en la recuperación. El tiempo estimado de baja puede estar entre las nueve y las 12 semanas. El base francés sufre un esguince en la rodilla derecha. Se lastimó en el primer cuarto del encuentro ante el Fenerbahce, cuando se le fue la articulación en una entrada a canasta. Pudo ser mucho peor. Enfiló el banquillo y siguió jugando, aunque en la segunda parte salió con una protección en la pierna. Podría tener que parar durante un mes. Más grave es lo del jugador finlandés, que se lesionó en el segundo cuarto sin sufrir torcedura ni golpe. Acudía al rebote de ataque en una jugada y segundos después ya estaba pidiendo el cambio. Había notado algo. Se fue cojeando al banquillo y allí fue explorado por miembros del servicio médico del equipo blanco. Después se levantó y, también cojeando, se marchó a los vestuarios para no volver a salir. Pedro Martínez advertía después del encuentro. "Parece un poquito grave. No tiene buena pinta", dijo el técnico, cuyos temores se han confirmado generándole un problema. Jantunen estaba siendo un jugador muy importante en los esquemas del Madrid más que por sus estadísticas, por su trabajo oscuro, su capacidad para abrir el campo con triples y por su polivalencia, pues estaba alternando los puestos de '4' y '5'. Las lesiones de Jantunen y Maledon se suman a las que padecen Usman Garuba, que va a perderse casi la totalidad de la temporada; Gabriel Deck, que estará unos cuatro meses de baja tras ser operado de un hombro; y Nick Smith Jr., que también arrastra problemas en la fascia plantar. La rotación del Madrid se queda aún más corta viendo que la adaptación de Max Shulga y Olivier Sarr va despacio y que el capitán Sergio Llull sólo tiene minutos en Liga Endesa. Este jueves entró en la convocatoria en Euroliga pero no llegó a jugar. En esa situación, con sólo 12 efectivos disponibles, los blancos estarían ya mirando el mercado en busca de algún refuerzo. Uno de los primeros nombres que han aparecido es el de Eli John Ndiaye. Después de que el Madrid igualara la oferta del Valencia Basket en el tanteo el pasado verano, el canterano está cedido en el Asisa Joventut, pero puede ser repescado después del 15 de noviembre si hubiera problema de cupos en las competiciones ACB. Ahora, sin contar al lesionado Usman Garuba, dispone de cinco: Llull, Alberto Abalde, Edy Tavares, Jaime Pradilla y un Shulga que podría salir cedido.

articles.title: Tiffany Hayes’ Dad calls out WNBA and Atlanta Dream over venue mishandling
articles.summary: Tiffany Hayes’ dad pulled no punches over the postseason arena scramble. The WNBA Finals went completely off the rails when Atlanta got caught flat-footed by...
articles.body:
Tiffany Hayes' dad pulled no punches over the postseason arena scramble.

The WNBA Finals went completely off the rails when Atlanta got caught flat-footed by venue conflicts. Gateway Center's tiny 3,500-seat capacity was never going to cut it, but with the Hawks hogging State Farm Arena that night, the league panicked.

Their band-aid fix? Squeezing the game into a bizarre 12:30 p.m. Thursday slot, forcing Bay Area fans to ditch work for a 9:30 a.m. tipoff.

Atlanta somehow didn't let the weird midday vibes throw them off, grinding out a gritty win over the Valkyries to send this wild series back to Chase Center for an epic Game 7.

Tiffany Hayes' Dad believes WNBA could have handled venue issue better

Tiffany Hayes' dad laid the blame right at the league's doorstep, slamming Atlanta and front-office execs for failing to plan ahead with the stadium . He pointed out how messy it looked to shove a championship game into the morning, leaving West Coast supporters out to dry.

On Outkick, he said:"It's kind of a shame about how they couldn't handle the situation better or couldn't be more prepared. They don't know that their teams are going to make the postseason, so they weren't prepared for this situation. But for us, it's okay. But for our fans in San Francisco, they're up at 930 in the morning, probably have to take a break off work, take the day off or whatever like that. But for me, I'm good with it.

"I think it's the league's fault. It's the league's fault and pretty much the Atlanta organisation because like last year, Golden State, when we made the playoffs, our second game had to be moved to a different arena, but it was almost the same size. It was in San Jose instead of San Francisco, but we were prepared for that. Instead of us here, they were talking about going to a 3,500-seat arena gateway. There's no way that game could have been completed or done. Some fans would have been upset about they couldn't make it or couldn't get in, couldn't get any tickets."

Game 7 goes down Sunday night at Chase Center, handing the Valkyries home-court edge with everything on the line. And to add to the occasion, it's the first Game 7 in WNBA history thanks to the league's new best-of-seven format.

articles.title: Tigers acquire middle infielder Tsung-Che Cheng from Red Sox
articles.summary: The Tigers have acquired left-handed hitting middle infielder Tsung-Che Cheng from the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
DETROIT — The Tigers have acquired left-handed hitting middle infielder Tsung-Che Cheng from the Boston Red Sox .

Per a report by Masslive,com and confirmed by The Detroit News, the Red Sox sent Cheng to the Tigers for cash considerations on Thursday, Oct. 29.

Cheng is 25 and was teammates with Tigers' Hao-Yu Lee for Chinese-Taipei in the World Baseball Classic last spring. He played in 14 games with the Red Sox last season, mostly at shortstop, hitting .256/.318/.282 with just one extra-base hit.

Interesting to note, the Red Sox won 13 of the 14 games that Cheng played.

In 94 games at Triple-A Worcester, Cheng hit .241/.345/.390 with a .735 OPS, the best of his three Triple-A seasons.

Interesting to see where he might fit into the crowded middle infield mix in Detroit, with Kevin McGonigle, Javier Báez and John Peck manning shortstop and Lee, Zach McKinstry and possibly Max Anderson at second.

articles.title: Casual basketball fans gobsmacked at horrible Angel Reese highlights from an actual WNBA Finals game
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries forced a WNBA Finals Game 7 as Angel Reese's tough Game 6 highlights go mega-viral across social media platforms.
articles.body: Here's the bad news: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream on Thursday to force a Game 7. The good news? Regardless of what happens on Saturday, there will be no more WNBA until next May. That's right. Our long, national nightmare of trans debates and Sophie Cunningham slander and national anthem nonsense will go into hibernation for seven glorious months. And, frankly, we've earned it. It's exhausting. This whole season has been exhausting. It's also been the longest season in the history of sports. It just won't end! FROM ANTHEMS TO DEFINITIONS, THE WNBA KEEPS DOING DUMB THINGS, AND THE REASON FOR IT WILL LEAVE YOU SPEECHLESS Now, don't get me wrong — I enjoyed the content during the summer months. It kept the lights on around here when there was no football. We needed a spark, and Sophie Cunningham gave us one because she's a patriot. God bless her. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ACTED LIKE AN ADULT THIS WEEKEND WHILE ANGEL REESE PANDERED, RED-HOT RED SOX & CUBS SMACK! Everyone else, though? I'm out on them. Thank goodness that league is on the doorstep of the offseason. It can't get here fast enough. Before we go, though, I do have one final collection of Angel Reese highlights that are currently going mega-viral on social media in the wake of yesterday's loss. Reese ... did not have her best game: Angel Reese has had a solid season, but Game 6 was a struggle Thoughts? First impressions? Look, it was a tough game for Angel Reese. No sugarcoating it. No hiding it. Just to show you how truly bad everyone else was, Reese somehow finished with a +/- of +10, which is stunning given she turned the ball over six times and made just 27% of her shots. Feels like that shouldn't equate to positive play on the court, but what do I know? Sometimes, you just have a tough day at the office. That's what Angel experienced yesterday afternoon in a potential close-out WNBA Finals game. And yes — there was an actual WNBA Finals game played at noon yesterday. Amazing. That's another story in itself, and one I don't care much about. What I do care about is Angel Reese. She was solid early on in these finals, but the last few games have been a struggle. Perhaps she's getting tired of having to field questions from OutKick's Dan Zaksheske every other night when the league actually grants us a question? CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE WNBA PLAYERS, COACHES REFUSE TO EXPLAIN NATIONAL ANTHEM ABSENCES AMID MOUNTING CRITICISM Could be. Or, perhaps the pressure-cooker that is the WNBA Finals is just getting to her? Seems like a real possibility. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Again, yesterday wasn't her best: Oh well. What's done is done. The series shifts back to Golden State for one final WNBA game in 2026. This one is for all the marbles, folks. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Will Angel rise to the moment? Will both teams disrespect our great national anthem for the 400th time? Will some gaslighting coach wear a "Trans Kids Lives Matters" shirt on the sideline? Better yet, will Angel wear another "Protect Black Women" shirt in 2026? articles.title: Yaxel Lendeborg has just made a change to his all-time NBA starting five

articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg has been the talk of the NBA so far this season.

The rookie has been magnificent for the Golden State Warriors so far this season, and many people already think he is destined for greatness.

Before he got to this stage, Lendeborg had his own heroes, and like the rest of us, he has an all-time NBA starting five.

However, the 24-year-old seems to have made a change to his lineup now.

Yaxel Lendeborg drops Kevin Durant from his all-time NBA starting five

We've all made changes to our all-time starting five in the NBA over the years, but Lendeborg's change has come in a short space of time.

In the first week of October, the Warriors rookie was interviewed by 95.7 The Game , where he was asked to name his best-ever starting five.

He replied at the time: "I'm going to go Steph [Curry]. I'm going to go Michael Jordan. I'm going to go LeBron [James]. Power forward… I think I might go KD [Kevin Durant] and Victor Wembanyama."

We're now in the final week of October, and after his brilliant start to the new NBA season, Lendeborg was asked the same question again on Kick .

This time, he took Durant out of his team.

Lendeborg said: "Steph Curry, Michael Jordan, LeBron James. I'm probably going to go… I might put Wemby at the four and Shaq at the five. Big a** line-up. You feel me?"

Pairing prime Shaq with Wemby at four and five creates a defensive frontcourt that effectively seals the lane. That forces opposing teams to do what they can purely from the outside.

Durant wouldn't be a bad option either, but we just feel that Lendeborg's starting five with Shaq is more balanced.
